name: VIP-safe webhook receiver
description: Adds a REST controller extending AbstractRESTController from rtcamp/wp-framework that receives signed JSON webhooks the way they survive at scale: it verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body in constant time, refuses every delivery until a shared secret is configured, caps the body size, acknowledges a retried delivery without queueing it twice, and hands the payload to a queue (Action Scheduler when loaded, WP-Cron otherwise) instead of doing the work inside the request. The secret is read from a VIP environment variable, or a constant of the same name elsewhere; it is never written by the scaffold.

inputs.description: PSR-4 namespace for the controller class. Default 'Inc\Rest' matches the rtCamp skeleton and wp/rest.
Directory for the controller file. Default 'includes/Rest'.

REST module file the controller is listed in. Default 'includes/Modules/Rest.php', the file `wp/module --name=Rest` creates. Pass the project's own file with its exact case, e.g. 'inc/Modules/REST.php' in features-plugin-skeleton: on a case-sensitive filesystem Rest.php is a different file.
PSR-4 namespace for the test class. Default 'Inc\Tests\Rest'.
Directory for the test file. Default 'tests/Rest'.
Webhook source, e.g. 'orders' or 'crm-contacts'. Used to derive the class, the route segment, the queued hook and the secret's name.
PascalCase class name prefix, derived from name. The controller is {class}WebhookController.
Route segment after /webhooks/, derived from name.
REST namespace prefix, e.g. 'myplugin'. The route becomes /wp-json/{rest_namespace}/v{rest_version}/webhooks/{route}.
Request header carrying the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body. Match your sender; adapt verify_signature() if it prefixes the digest or signs a timestamp too.
i18n text domain for error messages. Also prefixes the queued hook and the secret's name.
Prefix for the queued hook, derived from text_domain.
Source part of the queued hook, derived from name.
Prefix for the secret's environment variable or constant name, derived from text_domain.
Source part of the secret's name, derived from name.

wiring.description: Add the controller to the REST module so the framework Loader registers its route on rest_api_init. Edit the module file that exists, matching its case; if the project has none, scaffold it first via `wp-tooling add wp/module --name=Rest --kind=rest`. Deliveries are refused until the secret named by the controller's SECRET_NAME constant is set: as a VIP environment variable on VIP, or a constant in wp-config.php elsewhere. Process payloads in a job on the controller's HOOK, e.g. one from `wp-tooling add integration/vip-cron`.
